summary: Iran maintains closure of the Strait of Hormuz and rejects nuclear concessions while proposing a seven-day ultimatum for U.S. compliance to reopen talks. Israeli forces destroyed a two-kilometer Hamas tunnel in Gaza and killed two senior Hamas operatives involved in October 7 attacks and hostage-taking. Artillery and explosions continue across southern Lebanon as two Israeli reservists were killed in Gaza combat.
key_points: Iran's senior official tells Reuters the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until all Iranian conditions are met, with no nuclear talks or concessions planned (Source: @N12chat/227100).

IDF razed a two-kilometer tunnel in Israeli-held Gaza and killed Hamas commander Hassan Mahmoud Siam and operative Adham Sohbi Salim Ziara for violating ceasefire and planning attacks (Source: @manniefabian/59240).
Two IDF reservists from Battalion 7007, Brigade 16 were killed in Gaza combat: Nadav Kali, 24, and Ofek Moalem, 23 (Source: @New_security8200/203934).
Iranian FM Araghchi proposed a seven-day U.S. compliance window to reopen Hormuz and resume final agreement talks based on the Islamabad understanding (Source: @VahidOnline/78520).
IRGC-linked Fars News denies Axios and Al Jazeera reports of new Iran-U.S. talks, calling them fabricated to manage oil markets (Source: @shin_persian/10448).
Iraq suspended all flights to/from Iran at Najaf and Baghdad airports following U.S. sanctions on Iranian airlines, with UAE, Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan also complying (Source: @VahidOnline/78527).
Turkish Chief of Staff travels to Saudi Arabia for Mecca Defense Alliance meeting with Pakistan amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia (Source: @yediotnews25/135351).
Explosions and artillery fire reported across southern Lebanon with no cessation (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/394861).

sections.executive_summary: Iran refuses nuclear concessions and keeps the Strait of Hormuz closed pending a seven-day U.S. compliance ultimatum linked to the Islamabad understanding. Israeli forces eliminated a two-kilometer Hamas tunnel in Gaza and killed two senior operatives tied to October 7 hostage-taking, while two IDF reservists died in combat. Southern Lebanon experiences ongoing artillery and explosions as Iraq halts Iranian flights under U.S. sanctions pressure.

points: A senior Iranian official told Reuters the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed and no nuclear talks with the U.S. will occur until all Iranian conditions are met, explicitly ruling out any concessions on the nuclear program (Source: @N12chat/227100).

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated Iran delivered a proposal via intermediaries requiring the U.S. to implement specific conditions within seven days to reopen Hormuz and resume talks for a final agreement, saying conditions are "nothing more" than the Islamabad understanding which included sanctions relief, asset unfreezing, and cessation of military operations including in Lebanon (Source: @VahidOnline/78520).

President Pezeshkian in a Fox News interview expressed readiness for an agreement and reducing enriched uranium concentration but declined to specify nuclear stockpile locations or guarantee IRGC compliance, blaming the U.S. and Israel for killings of Iranian leaders and scientists (Source: @VahidOnline/78519).

IRGC-affiliated Fars News denied reports of new Iran-U.S. talks and of Iranian technical experts traveling to New York, calling the reports fabricated to manipulate markets and oil prices (Source: @shin_persian/10448).
Iran's Civil Aviation Authority confirmed the halt of flights to Iraq, ordering airlines to stop ticket sales and refund cancelled flights until further notice (Source: @shin_persian/10440).
Mohammad Mohseni, aide to Iran's leader, warned that if Iran cannot have flights and airport services, then no country in the region will either (Source: @asafroz/53785).

Former UK ambassador Matthew Gould wrote that five simultaneous factors are needed to overthrow Iran's government and the Trump administration must plan for post-transition governance (Source: @mamlekate/104626).

The IDF announced the destruction of a two-kilometer tunnel in the Israeli-held portion of the Gaza Strip as part of efforts to clear Hamas infrastructure from areas under Israeli control (Source: @manniefabian/59240).

Israeli strikes in Gaza City killed Hamas commander Hassan Mahmoud Siam, who participated in the October 7 invasion and held hostages Amit Soussana, Keith and Aviva Siegel, and Dafna Elyakim, and separately killed Hamas member Adham Sohbi Salim Ziara (Source: @shin_persian/10439).

The IDF stated both operatives were advancing attacks and restoring Hamas infrastructure in systematic violation of the ceasefire, including plans to fire at Israeli forces and plant explosives in the Yellow Line area (Source: @shin_persian/10439).
Two IDF reservists from Battalion 7007, Brigade 16 were killed in combat in Gaza: Nadav Kali, 24, from Har Halutz, and Ofek Moalem, 23, from Jerusalem (Source: @New_security8200/203934).

Security forces sealed the West Bank home of the terrorist who carried out the Neve Tzuf shooting attack that killed Netanel Shukron, ahead of planned demolition after the Central Command signed a temporary confiscation order (Source: @New_security8200/203938).
IDF engineering forces razed a two-kilometer tunnel in the Israeli-controlled area of the Gaza Strip, continuing clearance of Hamas military infrastructure (Source: @manniefabian/59240).

Hamas commander Hassan Mahmoud Siam and operative Adham Sohbi Salim Ziara were killed in separate Israeli strikes in Gaza City; the IDF accused them of ceasefire violations, attack planning, and planting explosives near the Yellow Line (Source: @shin_persian/10439).
Two IDF reservists from Battalion 7007, Brigade 16 died in Gaza combat, identified as Nadav Kali and Ofek Moalem (Source: @New_security8200/203934).

In the West Bank, IDF and Border Police under Benjamin Brigade sealed the home of the Neve Tzuf shooter in preparation for demolition after the terrorist was wounded and arrested during the attack (Source: @New_security8200/203938).
Continuous explosions and artillery fire are reported across southern Lebanon with no indication of cessation (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/394861).

Iran's proposed Islamabad understanding referenced by FM Araghchi includes cessation of military operations in Lebanon as a condition for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resuming nuclear talks (Source: @VahidOnline/78520).

Iraq's Civil Aviation Authority suspended all incoming and outgoing flights to/from Iran at Najaf International Airport from 2 AM Friday until further notice, citing official directives from relevant bodies (Source: @VahidOnline/78527).

Baghdad International Airport also halted Iranian flights; the measure follows U.S. sanctions on Iranian airlines, with UAE, Turkmenistan, and Azerbaijan also implementing restrictions (Source: @VahidOnline/78527).

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaydi directed the Transport Ministry to suspend Iranian flights after his office lacked authority to issue the ban directly; the Civil Aviation Authority holds exclusive jurisdiction over airport operations (Source: @naya_foriraq/91567).
Iraqi commentator Salah Al-Makhsusi criticized the flight ban as humiliating Iraq, cutting visits to holy sites, and prioritizing U.S. interests over Iraqi dignity (Source: @naya_foriraq/91605).
Turkish Chief of Staff will travel to Saudi Arabia for a Mecca Defense Alliance meeting with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, convened amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia (Source: @yediotnews25/135351).

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif declared the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb as vital global economic arteries that must remain open for prosperity, not war threats (Source: @SharghDaily/185782).
U.S. President Trump discussed Iran with Chinese President Xi Jinping, stating "very good things will happen" regarding reopening the Strait of Hormuz (Source: @mamlekate/104627).
A U.S. defense official told Al Jazeera that 60 tankers transited the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday despite Iranian closure threats (Source: @rodast_omiddana/81481).
Colombia designated the IRGC as a terrorist organization and increased border controls to prevent entry of IRGC-affiliated individuals (Source: @yediotnews25/135345).

key_developments: Iran's senior official tells Reuters the Strait of Hormuz stays closed and no nuclear talks will occur until all Iranian conditions are met, with zero concessions on the nuclear program (Source: @N12chat/227100).

IDF destroys a two-kilometer Hamas tunnel in Israeli-held Gaza and kills two senior Hamas operatives linked to October 7 hostage-taking and ceasefire violations involving Yellow Line explosives (Source: @manniefabian/59240).
Two IDF reservists from Battalion 7007, Brigade 16 killed in Gaza combat: Nadav Kali, 24, and Ofek Moalem, 23 (Source: @New_security8200/203934).

Iraq suspends all Iranian flights at Najaf and Baghdad airports under U.S. sanctions pressure; UAE, Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan also restrict Iranian carriers (Source: @VahidOnline/78527).

sections.threat_assessment: Iran's insistence on maintaining the Strait of Hormuz closure while linking its reopening to a seven-day U.S. compliance window creates a high-risk maritime flashpoint; the transit of 60 tankers Wednesday suggests neither side has yet enforced a full blockade. Israel's targeted elimination of Hamas commanders in Gaza and tunnel destruction indicates continued offensive operations despite ceasefire frameworks, risking escalation if Hamas retaliates. The simultaneous flight bans on Iranian carriers by Iraq and Gulf states under U.S. sanctions pressure deepen Iran's regional isolation and may provoke asymmetric responses. Ongoing artillery in southern Lebanon signals a fragile northern front that could ignite if Iran's Islamabad understanding conditions regarding Lebanese military operations are not addressed.
sections.regional_response: Saudi Arabia convenes the Mecca Defense Alliance with Turkey and Pakistan explicitly due to Houthi threats, signaling Gulf coordination against Iranian-backed proxies. Pakistan's prime minister publicly demands Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb remain open, aligning with global shipping interests. Colombia's IRGC terrorist designation extends international pressure beyond the Middle East. Iraq's compliance with U.S. sanctions on Iranian aviation, despite domestic criticism, demonstrates Baghdad's limited maneuverability. The U.S. reports constructive intermediary talks with Iran, but the seven-day ultimatum and Hormuz closure suggest a narrowing diplomatic window.
sections.intelligence_notes: The discrepancy between Iran's public denial of new talks (via Fars News) and Araghchi's detailed proposal to CNN suggests a dual-track messaging strategy: hardline domestic posture versus negotiated concessions. The specific mention of the Yellow Line in Gaza indicates Israeli focus on a defined security buffer zone. The Neve Tzuf shooter's home sealing follows standard IDF deterrence protocol but may inflame West Bank tensions. The Islamabad understanding's inclusion of Lebanese military cessation implies Iran seeks a comprehensive regional de-escalation package, not solely nuclear terms. Monitoring of tanker traffic through Hormuz will be the key real-time indicator of whether Iran enforces its closure threat.
